key_insight: Two new Lean 4 benchmarks show that current AI agents can prove some quantum algorithm and quantum information theorems, but performance is still uneven and strongly improved by access to verified libraries.
engineering_relevance: The benchmarks provide a reproducible way to measure and compare theorem-proving agents for quantum computing, helping identify where formal verification tools can realistically support quantum software and theory workflows.
method: Built Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench and Lean-QIT-Bench with 36 and 40 theorem-completion tasks
Evaluated GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, and MiniMax M3 in a common theorem-proving framework
Compared a task-only baseline against library-augmented deduction (LAD) using a verified domain library
evidence_signal: All tasks were checked by deterministic proof verification and semantic review, and LAD improved both score and completion rate across all eight model-benchmark comparisons, with top difficulty-weighted scores of 60.4 and 59.6.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific task design, so generalization to broader quantum theorem proving remains uncertain.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
